name: Auth0
desc: Hosted identity with social logins, MFA and enterprise SSO. Use when auth must be someone else's on-call rotation.

name: Clerk
desc: Drop-in auth with prebuilt React components and organisations. Use to have sign-in working in an afternoon.

name: Okta
desc: Enterprise workforce identity and SSO. Use when IT already owns the directory and you must plug into it.

name: WorkOS
desc: SAML, SCIM and directory sync as an API. Use the day your first enterprise customer demands SSO.

name: AWS Cognito
desc: AWS-native user pools and federated identity. Use when the rest of the stack is already AWS and IAM integration matters.

name: Stytch
desc: Passwordless-first auth: magic links, OTP and passkeys. Use when you want to delete the password field entirely.

name: Auth.js / NextAuth
desc: Self-hosted OAuth and session handling for JS apps. Use when you want social login without a vendor bill, and you have a database for sessions.

name: Keycloak
desc: Full open-source identity server with realms, SSO and federation. Use when data residency forbids a hosted provider.

name: SuperTokens
desc: Open-source auth you can host, with session management done properly. Use when you want Auth0 features under your own roof.

name: Lucia
desc: A reference for writing your own session auth rather than a library to install. Use when you want to understand and own every line.

name: Ory
desc: Composable identity, OAuth2 server and permission services in Go. Use for zero-trust architectures with fine-grained permissions.

name: Row Level Security
desc: Postgres policies that filter every query by the signed-in user, enforced inside the database. Use whenever browsers or apps query tables directly, as with Supabase, where a table without policies is readable by anyone holding the public key.

name: CASL
desc: Isomorphic permission rules shared by the API and the UI. Use when one can(user, 'update', post) check must both hide a button and guard the endpoint.

name: OpenFGA
desc: Zanzibar-style relationship-based access control you run as a service. Use for sharing models like Google Docs, where access follows folders, teams and organisations.

name: Permit.io
desc: Hosted RBAC, ABAC and ReBAC with a UI for editing roles. Use when product or support staff must change permissions without a deploy.

name: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC
desc: The delegation protocol behind every Sign in with button. Use as the default for third-party login.

name: SAML
desc: XML-based enterprise SSO. Use because large customers require it, never because you enjoy it.

name: JWT
desc: Signed stateless tokens. Use for service-to-service calls, and think twice before using them as revocable sessions.

name: Passkeys / WebAuthn
desc: Phishing-resistant login backed by device biometrics. Use to remove passwords and most support tickets with them.
